Wait — borrow issue: inside the block, `st.worlds.get_mut(&cur)` — st.scenario is a field of st; `let sc = st.scenario.clone();` then `st.worlds.get_mut` — fine.
But qing branch: after step_year, series push used `st.series.entry(cur)` — moved cur? In qing branch: `st.series.entry(cur).or_default()` — that moves cur! Then after if/else, `st.worlds.get_mut(&cur)` would use moved value → compile error. Look: qing branch line: `st.series.entry(cur).or_default().push(...)` vs standard branch: `st.series.entry(cur.clone()).or_default()`. The qing branch moves cur. So my block referencing cur after if/else fails for... no — it fails to compile regardless because cur moved in one branch. Fix: in block use `st.current.clone()` instead of cur:
